08/06/2018

Dr Barbara Jones
Dietician
Brightford General Hospital
Brightford

Dear Dr Jones,
Re: Rosemary McQueen, aged 15 years

I am writing to request your further management for Rosemary, who has recently been                                                     Commented [OETONLINE1]: Comma preferred as this is a
                                                                                                                                        non-defining relative clause
diagnosed with celiac disease.

Initially, Rosemary was seen two days ago in the Emergency Department when she
complained of persistent diarrhea with greasy stools, abdominal pain, and a blistering rash                                             Commented [OETONLINE2]: Use plural form of this word as
                                                                                                                                        more than one stool
over the elbows, the knees and the buttocks. In addition, she had lost 2.5 kg of weight in the
past previous two weeks and complained of easy bruising. Although her haematocrit,                                                      Commented [OETONLINE3]: Conjunction required for the last
                                                                                                                                        item in the list (which you have grouped)
calcium, WBC and platelets were low, PT and aPTT were high. A Sudan black stain was
                                                                                                                                        Commented [OETONLINE4]: Take care with time references
positive which indicates steatorrhea. All celiac antibody tests and a bowel biopsy confirmed                                            and making your writing formal
the diagnosis of celiac disease for which she was transferred to the paediatric unit.                                                   Commented [OETONLINE5]: Use capitals as this test is named
                                                                                                                                        after the country
Today, she is doing well and will be discharged. Regarding her discharge plan, she requires a
gluten-free diet, ferrous sulphate 200 mg for less than six months and to repeat the
antibody titers, CBC and calcium level after six weeks.
Missing paragraph: you needed to include the hc of f/hx of Chron’s disease ad possibly
diabetes in mother?
It would be greatly valued if you could take over Rosemary’s care and keep me updated on
the outcome. If you require any further clarification, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
